header: Date: 2026-03-29 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~55 min | Attendees: Marina (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Evan (Redwood), Priya (CISO), Liam (Cloud), Ana (Compliance), Marcus (Auditor)
summary: Internal audit readout: Verdant walked through current SOC 2/ISO gaps. Primary focus on key management, audit log retention, and trust center access. Redwood outlined KMS/HSM options, key rotation, RBAC for Trust Center, and evidence export. Action items agreed to share diagrams, schedule a hands-on KMS demo, and provide pricing for Dedicated with enhanced trust access.
topics: KMS / HSM integration and key rotation
RBAC and SSO for Trust Center
Dedicated vs Hosted for audit / data isolation
transcript:
[00:00] Marina (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We know Marcus had the internal audit readout today so we'll let you kick off. Quick intro, I'm Marina, AE on the account, Samir is our SE, Evan's here for notes.
[00:18] Marcus (Verdant Auditor): Thanks, yeah, Hi — I'm Marcus. We finished our internal SOC 2 mock last week, this call is to go through gaps we flagged and listen to Redwood's proposed KMS flow.
[00:30] Priya (CISO): Real quick — timeline, we need remediation evidence in 6 weeks for our external auditor. So speed matters.
[00:38] Samir (Redwood SE): Understood. We'll focus on the highest risk items — KMS and audit logs typically jump to top. Marcus, could you summarize top 3 gaps?
[00:52] Marcus: Sure. One — key rotation cadence and proof of rotation events; two — audit logs retention and access controls; three — evidence access for external auditors, we need time-bound read-only access plus RBAC.
[01:08] Ana (Compliance): Also, our control matrix flagged ambiguous owner assignments for a few infra controls that map to Redwood-hosted services. We need mapping that shows control owner and evidence artifacts.
[01:20] Evan (Redwood): Okay, we can provide a controls mapping doc that ties Redwood artifacts to your control IDs, and show where to pull raw logs.
[01:28] Liam (Cloud): Quick question on data residency — some datasets are EU-only due to GDPR. If we use Dedicated, can we guarantee EU-only tenancy?
[01:38] Samir: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned in an EU region with tenancy isolation. For hosted, we have routing policies but you'd need contractual data residency clauses.
[01:46] Priya: We prefer Dedicated for regulated data. Also need to confirm key material handling — do keys ever leave our KMS?
[01:54] Samir: We support BYOK with customer KMS keys; for Private deployments you can bring your own HSM. For hosted, we do envelope encryption where customer-managed keys can be used — keys do not leave the KMS; we hold wrapped keys.
[02:06] Marcus: Sorry, 'wrapped keys' — can you explain simply? Our auditor wants an event that shows a rotation happened.
[02:12] Samir: Sure. At a high level: the real data key is generated and encrypted (wrapped) by your KMS. Redwood never sees the plaintext. Rotation events are logged — we can emit an audit record each rotation and include a signature from the KMS.
[02:24] Marina: We'll share an architecture diagram showing the flow: app -> Redwood runtime -> data key encrypt/decrypt calls to KMS -> wrapped key stored with the model artifact.
[02:32] Priya: Do you support HSM-backed keys (i.e., FIPS 140-2/3)?
[02:36] Samir: Yes, we integrate with major cloud KMS providers with HSM protection; for on-prem we can integrate with an HSM via our private deployment options.
[02:44] Liam: How about KMS rotation cadence? Auditor expects quarterly rotation for certain keys.
[02:48] Samir: Rotation cadence is configurable at your KMS; we can show logs for every rotation event. We'll include sample log entries.
[02:56] Marcus: Logs — format? Our SOC 2 folks want immutable logs, SHA fingerprints, and an exportable bundle.
[03:02] Evan: We can push audit logs to your syslog endpoint or an S3 bucket with object lock for immutability. We emit JSON schema events with timestamps, request id, user id, key id, operation, and result.
[03:14] Ana: There's been occasional noise in transcripts, like 'KV cash' showing up; can you confirm log field naming is stable?
[03:20] Samir: Yeah sorry about that transcription — in logs we use consistent fields: request_id, model_id, operation, tokens_in, tokens_out, user_principal.
[03:30] Priya: On Trust Center access, we need read-only time-limited creds for external auditors. Does Redwood support time-bound roles?
[03:38] Samir: Yes — Trust Center supports short-lived SSO links (SAML/OIDC) that expire and can be scoped to read-only. We also have audit trails of who accessed which report.
[03:46] Marcus: Will the access show what artifacts were downloaded?
[03:50] Evan: Yes, we log downloads with user, timestamp, and artifact id.
[03:54] Marina: Another common ask: control mapping doc. We'll produce a CSV that maps your control ID -> Redwood artifact -> how to retrieve evidence.
[04:02] Ana: Good. For some controls we need chain-of-custody for keys. Can you provide signed rotation attestations?
[04:10] Samir: We can emit rotation attestations — basically an audit entry signed by your KMS or by Redwood's signing key showing key_id, previous_key_fingerprint, new_key_fingerprint, timestamp. If you use BYOK where your KMS signs, that's best.
[04:24] Priya: Competitor question — do other vendors keep more detailed low-level logs? I've heard MegaCloud AI keeps more kernel-level traces.
[04:32] Marina: Right, some vendors capture more telemetry, but that increases PII surface. Our approach is deliberate: we capture what you need for controls but avoid excess sensitive data.
[04:44] Liam: A bit of noise — can you explain disclaimers for hosted vs private regarding subpoena risk?
[04:50] Samir: Hosted is bound by Redwood's terms and data processing addendum; subpoenas to Redwood for hosted customer data are handled via legal channels, but with Private/Dedicated, you control the environment which reduces Redwood's access.
[05:04] Marcus: Can we get a sample Trust Center report PDF and the raw export?
[05:10] Evan: Yes, we can share a sample report plus the raw CSV/JSON export. We'll attach it to the follow-up.
[05:16] Ana: About RBAC — how granular can we be? We need role separation between ops, auditors, and devs.
[05:22] Samir: RBAC supports role definitions and attribute-based policies. You can map to SAML groups from your IdP and create custom roles that only allow read-only audit, read-only reporting, or admin deploy rights.
[05:34] Priya: SSO: do you support SCIM provisioning?
[05:36] Evan: Yes, SCIM provisioning is supported for user sync; SAML for SSO.
[05:40] Liam: For evidence exports, do you preserve original timestamps and timezone? Auditors like UTC.
[05:44] Samir: All audit timestamps are UTC and ISO-8601.
[05:48] Marcus: On retention, our control requires 1 year of immutable logs and 7 years for certain financial controls. Can Redwood guarantee that?
[05:56] Samir: We can set retention policies for exported logs. For hosted we have configured retention tiers; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and we can help with object lock in S3 for immutability.
[06:08] Priya: A specific ask — we need proof that key material is not backed up to any third party and is only in our KMS. How do you demonstrate that?
[06:18] Samir: With BYOK and HSM-backed keys, the raw key bytes are never exported. We can provide architecture docs and a runtime trace showing the KMS Decrypt call succeeded without plaintext leaving the KMS.
[06:30] Ana: Will that runtime trace expose user PII?
[06:34] Evan: We redact user-identifiable fields in the audit export if you want.
[06:38] Marcus: Ok. On controls mapping — we need someone from Redwood to walk through mapping for controls CC6, CC7, and ISMS-4. Could be technical but helpful.
[06:48] Marina: Samir can take that on and draft the mapping; we can have a follow-up 45-minute session with your compliance team.
[06:56] Samir: I'll prepare mapping rows with artifact links and example evidence pulls.
[07:02] Priya: Another question, how do you demonstrate separation of duties in the platform? For example, the person who deploys models shouldn't be able to change billing or audit logs.
[07:12] Samir: Role-based controls enforce that. Billing is a separate org-level permission; bulk log access requires a specific audit role. We can produce screenshots of role configs.
[07:22] Liam: Are logs tamper-evident? How do we detect manual edits?
[07:26] Evan: We support immutability options and can add cryptographic hashes on exported bundles. If you're using S3 object lock and MFA delete, combined with a signed index file, you get a tamper-evident archive.
[07:38] Marcus: For the auditor, a signed index file is helpful.
[07:42] Marina: Noted — we'll include an example signed index.
[07:46] Ana: Is there an integration for SIEMs? We use Splunk.
[07:50] Samir: We have native Splunk HEC support and generic syslog/CEF format exports.
[07:56] Priya: Off-topic but quick: model provenance — do you provide model hashes and version metadata?
[08:02] Samir: Yes, every model artifact in our registry has a content hash, version metadata, and provenance info (origin, quantization profile, training dataset tags where available).
[08:12] Marcus: That helps for change controls.
[08:14] Marina: We're at about 8 minutes in — actually 8? (laugh) — sorry, timestamps are approximate.
[08:20] (laughter)
[08:24] Samir: Let's run through a concrete KMS flow example — I'll describe and then Evan will show a sample log entry.
[08:32] Samir: Step 1: At init, the model container requests a data key from your KMS (GenerateDataKey). Step 2: The data key is used locally and the encrypted (wrapped) version is stored. Step 3: On rotation, the new key is generated and we update the wrapped key and emit a rotation event.
[08:50] Evan: Showing sample log: {"ts":"2026-03-15T12:03:21Z","req_id":"r-8a7f","user":"svc-infer","op":"kms:GenerateDataKey","key_id":"arn:aws:kms:eu:...","result":"success"}
[09:06] Ana: That looks good. Can we have the sample include the KMS key fingerprint in the log?
[09:10] Evan: Yes, we can add key_fingerprint.
[09:14] Priya: For external auditors, would you provide a signed bundle including logs and rotation attestations?
[09:20] Samir: Yes, we can create an export bundle signed by Redwood and optionally include your KMS-signed rotation attestations if you enable BYOK.
[09:30] Marcus: What about retention of redaction rules? We sometimes need to redact PII for auditors.
[09:36] Samir: Our export pipeline can apply redact rules pre-export, and we can also provide raw unredacted exports to a customer-controlled S3 if you want full forensic detail.
[09:46] Liam: Does that mean Redwood won't have the unredacted logs if we choose to store them in our bucket?
[09:50] Evan: Correct — if you configure the export to your S3, Redwood won't store that copy.
[09:56] Priya: Ok good. Next: control evidence delivery cadence — Ana's team wants weekly snapshots of key controls for 6 weeks. Can Redwood automate snapshots?
[10:06] Samir: Yes, we can automate scheduled exports of selected evidence bundles. We can name them with timestamps and ship to your S3 with object lock.
[10:14] Ana: For the demo, we'd like to see a snapshot with object lock enabled.
[10:18] Marina: We'll include that in the hands-on KMS demo.
[10:22] Marcus: One last technical item — for cryptographic signing of logs, who holds the signing key?
[10:28] Samir: We can sign with Redwood's signing key for convenience, but for highest assurance we recommend you sign with your key in your KMS. We can surface the payload so you can sign client-side and then we store the signed index in the archive.
[10:40] Priya: That aligns with our policy — we prefer to sign.
[10:44] Marina: Ok I'll summarize next steps: Samir will draft KMS playbook and control mapping, Evan will attach sample logs and Trust Center sample report, and I'll send pricing for Dedicated+Trust access.
[10:56] Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers?
[11:00] Marcus: None immediate. We'll await the artifacts and schedule the demo week of 4/13.
[11:06] (crosstalk)
[11:08] Samir: Quick note — you mentioned financial controls requiring 7-year retention; we'll work with your infra team on long-term archival.
[11:16] Ana: I'll prepare the internal control list and share by Monday.
[11:20] Marina: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[11:24] Priya: Thanks.
[11:26] Marcus: Thanks all.
[11:28] Evan: Bye.
[11:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional transcription errors observed ('KV cash' for KV cache, 'H S M' spelled out), attendee names sometimes shortened. Shared artifacts to follow: sample Trust Center PDF, KMS flow diagram, sample audit log JSON, draft controls mapping CSV.
